articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the first issue of the third volume of "SJAA Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It was published in January 1992, serving as a periodical for the association's members.

articles.title: January Speaker
articles.summary: The January speaker will be architect Ethan Wilson Cliffton, an expert in complex observatory design with extensive experience on projects like the Keck Observatory, NASA Space Station, and Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory. He will discuss his work and provide guidance for the SJAA observatory project, covering aspects such as thermal, vibration, and radiation isolation, mirror technology, and aerodynamics. The document also details upcoming January and February events, including star parties at various locations, general meetings, and beginning astronomy classes.

articles.title: FROM YOUR EDITOR
articles.summary: The editor addresses newsletter numbering conventions, establishing each year as a Volume and each month as a No., while also making a plea for new articles and help with drawing maps to observing sites. The issue features the start of a multi-part talk by C. Tombaugh and reminds members of a change in meeting location to the Milpitas Library. The article also lists the current officers of the organization.

articles.title: WHAT'S IN A DOME
articles.summary: This article discusses the design features for the new Halley Hill Dome, which is intended to be a site-independent, amateur-built observatory dome available to astronomers everywhere. The author, Del Jonson, solicits input on design specifics, listing ten suggested features ranging from power provisions and storage to dome rotation options and sizing for a 12.5" f6 Newtonian. Readers are encouraged to contact Del Jonson with additional suggestions.

articles.title: Henry Coe State Park Star Party
articles.summary: A star party held at Henry Coe State Park was significantly impacted by strong, persistent winds, gusting up to 25 MPH, despite initially clear skies. Attendees faced challenges with dust, cold, and poor observing conditions that made celestial objects like the Trapezium difficult to focus, leading some to leave early. Despite the difficult weather, several participants had set objectives to observe various deep-sky objects, galaxies, nebulae, clusters, and planets like Jupiter.

articles.title: Lunar Phases Date Rise Tran Set
articles.summary: This document outlines the schedule for major lunar phases within a given month. It provides specific dates and times for the New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, and Last Quarter, alongside their corresponding rise, transit, and set times.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for several 'nearer planets' including Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, alongside data for the Sun (SOL), across specific dates. For each celestial body, it lists its distance in Astronomical Units (A.U.), apparent visual magnitude (Mag), and three daily time points likely representing rise, transit, and set times. This information serves as a practical guide for observers to track and locate these objects.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document is a concise reference detailing specific dates and corresponding start and end times for astronomical twilight. It presents these periods using Julian Dates and Gregorian calendar dates, indicating when the sky is sufficiently dark for astronomical observations.

articles.title: Sidereal Time
articles.summary: This document provides specific astronomical timing data for January, including Sidereal Time values for Transit Right, Ascensionan, and Local Midnight. It also details the sunset, twilight end, and moonset times for a designated "Darkest Saturday Night" on January 4th, all presented in Pacific Standard Time (PST).

articles.title: TIMES & DATES ARE PACIFIC STANDARD
articles.summary: This document snippet, authored by Richard Stanton, serves as a preface stating that all listed times and dates are in Pacific Standard Time. It references an ephemeris for January 1992, indicating the presence of astronomical data or celestial predictions for that month, likely found on a subsequent page.

articles.title: Dr. Clyde Tombaugh's talk to the EAS
articles.summary: In a 1989 talk to the Eastbay Astronomical Society, Dr. Clyde Tombaugh recounts the history of planet discoveries, including Uranus and Neptune, often highlighting the challenges and amusing 'blunders' made. He then shares his personal journey to Lowell Observatory, the arduous task of searching through millions of star images on photographic plates, and the ultimate thrill of discovering Pluto, an object he describes as incredibly dim and elusive.

articles.title: Double, Triple, and Multiple Stars
articles.summary: This article explores various double, triple, and multiple star systems within the constellation Lepus, offering specific observational targets for amateur astronomers. It details star magnitudes, separations, and types (true vs. optical companions) for systems like Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Leporis, h3780 (NGC 2017), and h3752, along with a mention of the globular cluster M-79. The author also provides practical observing advice, such as viewing objects near the meridian for improved clarity.

articles.title: February Speaker
articles.summary: This article announces a talk by Dr. David Schramm, co-author of "Shadows of Creation," at the February 8th general meeting at the Milpitas Library. Dr. Schramm will discuss contemporary cosmology, covering topics such as the Big Bang vs. Steady State Universe debate, and the universe's potential end scenarios (Big Chill or Big Crunch), emphasizing the role of dark matter. The event is arranged by Bob Garfinkle.

articles.title: Grant Ranch Star Party
articles.summary: A star party was held at Grant Ranch on Saturday, December 7th. Despite early overcast conditions, the sky cleared up, allowing participants to observe celestial objects like M-1 and the Trapezium using various telescopes and binoculars. The event was well-attended, with several individuals bringing their equipment for a successful outing.

articles.title: Fremont Peak outing
articles.summary: An excellent stargazing outing occurred at Fremont Peak on Sunday, December 8th, under exceptionally clear sky conditions rated 8/10. Attendees, including Paul Barton with his 18" JMI and Dan and Chris Wright with a 12.5" Dob, observed celestial objects such as four stars in the Trapezium and a wide-split Gamma Andromedae. They attempted to view the Horse Head Nebula but lacked an H-II filter.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document, "ASTRO ADS," serves as a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products and services. It features numerous listings for used telescopes (e.g., Celestron 14, C-8, C-5), optical components, and accessories, alongside CCD images and a celestial globe. Additionally, the section includes announcements for an astronomy convention (COSMOCON 92), a new catalog of astronomy materials, and a personal ad seeking a travel companion for an astronomy-focused trip.

articles.title: The Presidential Papers
articles.summary: The author, Jeff Z., reflects on the importance of community and astronomy during challenging economic times, urging participation in SJAA's public outreach events. He details a successful winter observing session at Fremont Peak where he, using a 30" reflector, resolved Gamma Andromeda as a triple star and thoroughly explored the Orion Nebula. The article concludes with an update on fundraising for a solar H-alpha filter to enhance public programs.

articles.title: SPECIAL NOTICE
articles.summary: This special notice announces a permanent change in the general meeting site to the Milpitas Library, effective January 1992. It provides detailed directions to the new location from both 880 (17) and 680. Additionally, it previews upcoming speakers for February and March, including Ethan Clifton discussing an observatory project, Dr. Schramm on Cosmology, and Shilo Unruh from Lick Observatory.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current offices and Board of Directors for an organization. It provides the names, titles (President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and Directors), and contact phone numbers for each board member.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists the names and contact phone numbers of individuals who contribute to an ephemeris, as well as the contact information for its editor. It appears to be an internal contact list for the editorial and contributing team members.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document, titled "EPHEMERIDES," provides detailed astronomical positional data for three periodic comets: Hartley 2 (1991t), Faye (1991n), and Shoemaker-Levy (1991d). For each comet, tables list their Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation, sky visibility (Morning or Evening), and predicted Magnitude across various dates from late December through early February. This information serves as a practical guide for astronomers to track and observe these celestial objects.

articles.title: Comet Commets
articles.summary: Don Machholtz reports on the recent discoveries of two new comets, Shoemaker-Levy 6 (1991b) and Shoemaker-Levy (1991d), along with the recovery of Tsuchinshan 1 (1991c). He also notes three faint comets remain visible and announces a shift to providing only Epoch 2000 coordinates for comets moving forward, for the benefit of visual observers.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document outlines membership information for the San Jose Astronomical Association, specifically regarding their monthly publication, EPHEMERIS. Members are invited to submit typed articles for publication by the 12th of the preceding month, sent to the editor, Bob Madden, at the provided address.

articles.title: Membership only: $10 Membership/S&T: $28 Junior (under 18): $18
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing different membership options and their costs: Membership only ($10), Membership/S&T ($28), and Junior (under 18) ($18). It includes instructions for submitting the form and payment to the treasurer, Jack Peterson, at the SJAA's Milpitas address, and also lists contact information and a hotline number. The document is dated January 1992.
